articles.summary: Voters in Sunday's election are choosing between two very different candidates, as Americas correspondent Ione Wells reports from Rio de Janeiro.
articles.body:

They are choosing between Brazil's current left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and the right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

articles.title: I've been to Costa Rica more than 30 times. These are the rookie mistakes that can turn a dream vacation into a headache.
articles.summary: These first-timer tips will help ensure you come back with positive memories — not regrets.
articles.body:
I've made more than 30 trips to Costa Rica, so I've had plenty of chances to make my share of mistakes, from under-budgeting and over-scheduling to wasting precious luggage space on the wrong gear. I've also booked subpar accommodations to save some money, only to end up spending more on a last-minute place to stay.

Of course, part of the joy of travel is the lessons you learn along the way. Some mistakes are minor, laughable and fixable — and might even lead to new experiences or friendships. But some mistakes could cost you time and money, put off local people or even put your safety at risk. Read on for my list of the most common first-timer mistakes.

Costa Rica is not the only place with a San José airport. If your dream destination is Costa Rica, not Silicon Valley, double-check that your flight is headed to SJO (the airport code for Juan Santamaría International Airport near San José), not SJC (the San José Mineta International Airport in San José, California), before you book.

Also, when searching for flights, don't forget that Costa Rica has another international airport in Guanacaste: the Daniel Oduber Quirós International Airport, also known as the Liberia International Airport (LIR) or the Guanacaste Airport. Depending on your itinerary, flying into LIR could shorten your journey, particularly if you're visiting Guanacaste or the northern Pacific coast.

Costa Rica doesn't look that big on a map, so you might assume you can cover the whole country in your one or two-week visit. But varying topography, winding (and sometimes narrow and rough) roads and changing weather conditions mean drives tend to take longer than they look on a map.

Cattle and wildlife (the rumor is true: Traffic stops to let sloths cross!), road repairs and accidents can also cause delays. On a recent trip, we sat in the same spot for an hour, just minutes away from reaching our hotel, because part of the road was being repaired and there wasn't enough room to pass. A car ride we thought would take under an hour took twice as long.

Avoid over-scheduling your itinerary, build in a buffer time and assume drives will take longer than the GPS says. If you've only got one week in Costa Rica, pick just one or two regions to visit. Otherwise, you'll spend more of your vacation in the car than at the beach or in the rainforest.

So you checked the weather forecast for your travel dates and it's showing rain every day. Now, you're panicking. While it may indeed rain every day, depending on when and where you're going, there's a good chance it won't rain all day, every day.

Costa Rica's tropical climate and multiple microclimates across the country mean it does rain often, but not everywhere all the time. You'll generally get a mix of sun and showers — and that may not match what the forecast shows.

It's smart to keep an eye on the news and weather, especially during the rainy season , when storms can cause flooding and road closures. But don't obsess over it. If you want to experience Costa Rica, part of that is experiencing it in all types of weather — and being able to roll with it. If you've got your rain jacket, a positive, flexible attitude and a backup plan (hot springs are heavenly in the rain, but there are plenty of indoor activities, like cooking classes too), you're going to have a great time, rain and shine.

Speaking of the weather, a lot of travelers avoid the rainy season (May through November), also known as the green season. But it can be a good time to visit Costa Rica if you're into cooler temperatures, greener landscapes, fewer crowds, coastal hikes and surfing. Also, the Caribbean side tends to have a bit less rain in September and October, which are the wettest months on the Pacific side.

As mentioned above, the weather in Costa Rica can be tricky to pin down. It might still rain during your dry season trip, and it could be sunny if you visit during the green season. When I was living in Guanacaste, we got hit with several rainstorms during the dry season months. And on a different trip to Costa Rica in the middle of the green season, I hiked under clear blue skies.

One of my friends who visited Costa Rica recently told me she didn't see much wildlife. I was shocked, but then realized why: She never hired a guide during her trip. The forests in Costa Rica are dense, and if you don't know what you're looking for or where to look, you can easily miss some incredible creatures. Trained guides have the keen eye, knowledge and equipment needed to find even the teeniest and most elusive species.

Some of my most vivid memories of Costa Rica over the years have been moments when a guide spotted something I would have never noticed on my own, including the time a guide found a tiny emerald toucanet, camouflaged by the foliage in Mistico Park , and another instance when a guide suddenly stopped the car to show us a little bitty eyelash viper on a fence alongside the road that we were whizzing by.

Letting your fears limit your experience

Costa Rica is home to an abundance of wildlife, and for some people, that can be intimidating. Yes, there are snakes, lizards, spiders and many other creatures here. But rather than trying to avoid them completely, consider learning about them instead.

I had a pretty sizable fear of snakes before spending time in Costa Rica. But I seemed to encounter them regularly (one time, I was joking with a guide at Braulio Carrillo National Park about snakes showing up wherever I go in the world, and one crossed the trail between us at that exact moment!).

I decided I'd better accept my snake magnetism and get more comfortable with them. So I started replacing my fear with curiosity; I asked guides more questions about snake identification and their roles in the ecosystem, and I joined snake identification groups where people share photos, videos and distinct features and behaviors. I can't say I'm completely fearless now, but I am better informed, which has made me more comfortable traveling in Costa Rica.

Not packing closed-toe shoes and warm layers

Sandals and swimsuits are great for the beach. But if you're planning to visit the mountainous regions and do any hiking, ziplining, ATV-ing, horseback riding or other outdoor adventures, you'll need more coverage.

Some outdoor activities require closed-toe shoes for safety, and areas at higher elevations, such as the cloud forests of Monteverde , can get chilly at night. Skip the cotton and denim and go for quick-dry materials. You might not imagine needing wool socks or a sweater on your Costa Rica vacation, but wool is moisture-wicking and odor-resistant — two things you want in your hiking gear.

Sometimes when we leave home, our brains switch to vacation mode too. Costa Rica has all the ingredients of a tropical paradise, but there are also common risks, and it's wise to keep your wits about you.

Leave valuables at home; always lock your accommodations and car (even if you're only running into the store for a moment); don't be flashy with money or jewelry; and pay attention to your surroundings rather than being distracted by your phone. Some short-term rentals have been targeted by burglars, so I personally recommend sticking to vetted hotels and other properties with robust security.

Bring your common sense along on your outdoor adventures too. Always heed the guide's instructions, stay away from rivers during and after rainstorms (flash flooding can be sudden and dangerous) and watch where you step, lean and sit. Most creatures in Costa Rica aren't aggressive, but they don't take kindly to being startled and may sting or bite.

I keep two memories front of mind to keep me from leaning or sitting willy-nilly without looking: I picture the bullet ants (who pack a painful punch if they sting you) crossing a log I almost sat on, and a tiny green viper that was curled up, napping on a leaf right next to a trail. Had guides not pointed these out on my early trips to Costa Rica, I likely wouldn't have seen them and could have unintentionally disturbed them — and suffered the consequences.

Expecting things to be as they are where you're from

The quickest way to wear out your welcome? Expecting everything in Costa Rica to be the same as where you're from. Things tend to be more laid-back here, and the official language is Spanish, so not everyone will be perfectly punctual or speak English. Learn at least a few Spanish phrases and get on board with leaning into a looser schedule.

articles.title: Could Israel’s military crackdown influence Tuesday’s election?
articles.summary: Israel preparing a full lockdown of occupied West Bank after Hebron gunfight.
articles.body:
Two Israeli soldiers were killed in a shooting near Hebron on Friday morning.

Israel is responding with a sweeping military operation and a lockdown across the occupied West Bank.

Palestinians accuse Israel of collective punishment, as entire communities are placed under lockdown, families forced from their homes and buildings are demolished.

And with Israeli elections just days away, far-right politicians are seizing on the attack to push for annexation and tougher policies against Palestinians.

So, could this crackdown influence the election?

And is it genuinely about security, or is this being used as an opportunity to expand Israel’s occupation of Palestinian territory?

articles.summary: Uma policial e uma colaboradora ficaram feridas após acidente com urnas eletrônicas no Amazonas, enquanto o TRE avalia danos aos equipamentos de votação.
articles.body:
Acidente com veículo que transportava urnas eletrônicas deixa duas mulheres feridas no AM — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Duas mulheres ficaram feridas em um acidente com um veículo que transportava urnas eletrônicas para as Eleições 2026, neste sábado (24), em Lábrea , no interior do Amazonas. As condições dos equipamentos são avaliadas pelo Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Amazonas (TRE-AM).

Segundo o tribunal, o acidente ocorreu nas proximidades da Vila Campina Grande, na comunidade Remansinho. As vítimas são uma policial e uma colaboradora da Justiça Eleitoral.

As duas estavam conscientes e foram levadas ao hospital de Acrelândia, no Acre, para avaliação médica e realização de exames. De acordo com as informações preliminares, os demais ocupantes do veículo não se feriram.

O TRE-AM avalia as condições das urnas eletrônicas transportadas para verificar se será necessário substituir algum equipamento e garantir a continuidade dos procedimentos eleitorais.

articles.title: Aos 89 anos, idosa que viveu ditadura no Brasil faz questão de votar | G1
articles.standfirst: Moradora de Urupês (SP), Else Pazin foi às urnas no 1º turno em 4 de outubro e está ansiosa para exercer novamente o papel de cidadã neste domingo (25).
articles.summary: Aos 89 anos, uma idosa que viveu o período da ditadura militar no Brasil faz questão de votar em Urupês, no interior de São Paulo.
articles.body:
Aos 89 anos, uma idosa que viveu o período da ditadura militar no Brasil faz questão de votar em Urupês , no interior de São Paulo.

Else Pazin foi às urnas no 1º turno em 4 de outubro e revelou ao g1 que está ansiosa para exercer novamente o papel de cidadã neste domingo (25), durante o 2º turno do pleito.

Dona Else, aos 89 anos, foi votar no 1º turno das eleições um Urupês (SP) — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

"Eu acho isso importante, por quê? Nós somos cidadãos, nós precisamos tomar uma atitude sobre as eleições", comenta a eleitora.

Neste ano, a taxa de abstenção no 1º turno das eleições ultrapassou os 33,4 milhões de eleitores — 21,08% do eleitorado apto a votar — e atingiu o nível mais alto desde 1998. No total, nove estados ficaram acima da média nacional. São Paulo teve 7.687.443, o que representou 22,56% do eleitorado.

Else pontua as dificuldades enfrentadas pela população durante o período de 21 anos do regime autoritário no país, entre 1964 e 1985, até a redemocratização. Segundo ela, deixar de votar nos dias atuais é algo inadmissível.

"Poder votar é uma coisa maravilhosa. É possível ajudar o Brasil a melhorar e ser mais forte. Tenho coragem e aconselho minhas amigas a também terem a mesma iniciativa", pontuou Pazin.

Else Pazin vota em Urupês (SP) — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Dados do Senado Federal apontam que o número de eleitores idosos cresceu cerca de 14% desde as eleições de 2022, alcançando neste ano 37,5 milhões de aptos a votar. As pessoas idosas representam 23,6% de todo o eleitorado nacional.

"Não adianta dizer assim: 'Não vou votar não, porque eu já tenho idade'. Idade não interessa, o que interessa é a cabeça. Então, eu estou boa da cabeça, lembro dos meus candidatos e eu vou votar", afirma Else.

A Justiça Eleitoral recomenda que os eleitores levem os números dos candidatos anotados em um papel para facilitar a votação — Foto: Clara Abrami

Um levantamento do Movimento Voto 70+ em colaboração com o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) elucida que o percentual de eleitores nessa faixa etária que não foram votar passou de 58,8% em 2022 para 49,1% no primeiro turno de 2026.

Prestes a completar 90 anos em 8 de novembro, Else diz que sempre é parabenizada por mesários e por outros eleitores quando chega à Escola Municipal Maria da Gloria Robert Lima de Almeida, onde exerce o voto.

"Quando eu chego aos lugares para votar, as pessoas se levantam e me dão os parabéns", finalizou a aposentada.

articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada neste sábado (24) é a última antes do 2º turno, neste domingo, e foi encomendada pela Globo e pela Folha de S.Paulo.
articles.summary: Pesquisa divulgada neste sábado (24) é a última antes do 2º turno, neste domingo, e foi encomendada pela Globo e pela Folha de S.Paulo.
articles.body:
Pesquisa Datafolha divulgada neste sábado (24), véspera do segundo turno, mostra como está a disputa pelo governo do Distrito Federal.

O levantamento indica a atual governadora do DF, Celina Leão ( PP ), como favorita para ser reeleita.

Celina Leão e Leandro Grass — Foto: Ingrid Ribeiro/TV Globo e Amanda Sales/TV Globo

O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo e pela Folha de S. Paulo e ouviu 1.620 eleitores de 16 anos ou mais , entre os dias 23 e 24 de outubro . A margem de erro é de 2 pontos percentuais , para mais ou para menos. O nível de confiança é de 95% . A pesquisa foi registrada na Justiça Eleitoral sob o número DF-03453/2026 .

É a forma como o TSE divulga o resultado oficial das eleições. São os votos dados nos candidatos. Esse cálculo deixa de fora os votos em branco e nulos e abstenções. Para vencer no 1º turno, um candidato precisa de 50% dos votos válidos mais um voto.

Nas pesquisas, as empresas excluem os votos em branco e nulos e os eleitores indecisos para calcular os votos válidos.

Veja agora o resultado com os votos totais, incluindo votos em branco, nulos e eleitores indecisos.

Celina Leão (PP): 54% (eram 54% no levantamento anterior, em 22 de outubro );

Veja agora a pesquisa espontânea, em que os eleitores respondem sem ter acesso a uma lista de candidatos.

Esses resultados ajudam a medir o grau de consolidação do voto. Quanto maior o número de indecisos na véspera, menos consolidado está o voto e maior a possibilidade de mudanças em relação ao resultado de domingo.

Celina Leão (PP): 47% (eram 47% em 22 de outubro);

Branco/nulo/não vai votar: 5% (eram 7%);

Vota no PT / no candidato do PT: 1% (era 1%).

Entre os eleitores que declaram voto em um candidato, 92% dizem que a decisão é definitiva. Outros 7% afirmam que ainda podem mudar de ideia.

articles.title: Ademar Cardoso, irmão de Djidja, deixa a prisão em Manaus | G1
articles.standfirst: Ademar cumpre uma pena de 10 anos e 11 meses de prisão pelos crimes de tráfico de drogas e associação para o tráfico, estando preso desde maio de 2024, dias após Djidja ser encontrada morta dentro da casa da família com sinais de overdose de cetamina.
articles.summary: Ademar Cardoso, irmão de Djidja Cardoso, progrediu para o regime semiaberto com tornozeleira eletrônica após condenação por tráfico na Operação Mandrágora.
articles.body:
Ademar Cardoso, irmão da ex-sinhazinha do Boi Garantido Djidja Cardoso , deixou o presídio na manhã deste sábado (24) para cumprir pena em regime semiaberto, em Manaus . A Justiça do Amazonas autorizou a progressão de regime na sexta-feira (23) , com a determinação do uso de tornozeleira eletrônica e o cumprimento de regras, como o recolhimento noturno .

Ademar cumpre uma pena de 10 anos e 11 meses de prisão pelos crimes de tráfico de drogas e associação para o tráfico, estando preso desde maio de 2024, dias após Djidja ser encontrada morta dentro da casa da família com sinais de overdose de cetamina .

Após sair da prisão, Ademar foi recebido por amigos e familiares. Vídeos publicados nas redes sociais do salão de beleza Belle Femme mostram o momento em que ele cumprimenta Verônica da Costa Seixas, também condenada no processo relacionado à Operação Mandrágora, e falou com a imprensa.

Em uma das gravações, Ademar afirma que pretende apresentar sua versão sobre o caso, mas que vai conversar com os advogados antes de dar mais detalhes.

"Agora é a minha vez de mostrar o outro lado da moeda. Toda história tem três versões: a do lado deles, a minha e a verdadeira. Somente eu sei a verdade, então estou disposto a falar sobre isso com muita cautela, muita calma. Eu acabei de sair da cadeia, passei dois anos, dois anos e meio, basicamente sem visita, sem nada. Passei esses anos todos estudando, meditando, orando e estou praticamente preparado para qualquer tipo de pergunta. Não vai ser agora, então ainda vou conversar com meus advogados", afirmou.

Ademar também agradeceu aos advogados, amigos e familiares pelo apoio durante o período em que esteve preso. Em outra declaração, voltou a contestar a prisão.

"Eu vou simplesmente destrinchar tudo para vocês, porque fui preso, na minha opinião, ilegal e arbitrariamente", declarou.

Irmão de Djidja Cardoso deixa presídio e é recebido por amigos e pela mãe em Manaus — Foto: Foto: Reprodução/Rede Sociais

Depois da recepção, Ademar foi para casa, onde reencontrou a mãe, Cleusimar Cardoso. Em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, ela aparece na porta da residência com um buquê de girassóis e uma caixa de bombons. Os dois se abraçam.

Cleusimar também deixou a prisão após conseguir a progressão para o regime semiaberto, em 29 de setembro . Na ocasião, foi recebida por amigos e funcionários do salão Belle Femme, que administrava ao lado da filha.

A decisão que autorizou a progressão de pena de Ademar foi proferida pela juíza Sabrina Cumba Ferreira nesta sexta-feira (23). Ele cumpre pena de 10 anos e 11 meses de prisão por tráfico de drogas e associação para o tráfico.

Pelo cálculo inicial da execução penal, Ademar só teria direito à progressão para o semiaberto em outubro de 2027. No entanto, a data foi antecipada para outubro de 2026 após a Justiça reconhecer o abatimento de 364 dias da pena.

Segundo a decisão, ele cumpriu os requisitos de tempo de prisão e bom comportamento exigidos pela Lei de Execução Penal. A redução da pena considerou a participação em atividades de trabalho, leitura e estudo na unidade prisional, incluindo a aprovação no Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) de 2025.

O exame criminológico, realizado por uma comissão multiprofissional, também apontou capacidade de autocontrole, discernimento e aptidão para o retorno gradual à sociedade. O Ministério Público do Amazonas (MPAM) emitiu parecer favorável à progressão.

Para cumprir a pena em regime semiaberto, Ademar deverá usar tornozeleira eletrônica e seguir as condições estabelecidas pela Justiça.

Recolhimento noturno : permanecer em sua residência das 22h às 6h nos dias úteis, podendo sair apenas para trabalhar, estudar ou fazer tratamento de saúde;

Fins de semana e feriados : recolher-se integralmente em casa;

Viagens e mudança : não mudar de endereço nem se ausentar de Manaus sem autorização prévia da Justiça;

Proibições : não ingerir bebidas alcoólicas, não usar drogas ilícitas e não portar nenhum tipo de arma.

Ademar foi condenado em 22 de julho de 2026, junto com outras seis pessoas , em uma nova sentença relacionada ao esquema investigado pela Operação Mandrágora.

Também foram condenados Cleusimar Cardoso, José Máximo Silva de Oliveira, Hatus Moraes Silveira, Verônica da Costa Seixas, Sávio Soares Pereira e Bruno Roberto da Silva Lima.

As penas dos sete condenados variaram de oito anos e seis meses a 10 anos e 11 meses de prisão.

Segundo a sentença, o grupo utilizava a rede de salões de beleza Belle Femme e a seita religiosa "Pai, Mãe, Vida" para distribuir e aplicar cetamina . A substância é usada como anestésico veterinário e, segundo a investigação, era obtida de forma ilegal e utilizada em rituais do grupo.

Outros três réus — Emicley Araújo Freitas, Claudiele Santos da Silva e Marlisson Vasconcelos Dantas — foram absolvidos por falta de provas suficientes.

A condenação de julho foi uma nova decisão sobre o mesmo processo. A sentença anterior havia sido anulada pela Justiça 10 meses antes .

Depois da regularização das provas periciais, a Justiça entendeu que havia elementos suficientes para confirmar os crimes e a responsabilidade dos condenados.

Djidja Cardoso, empresária e ex-sinhazinha do Boi Garantido que morreu por suspeita de overdose — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

Djidja Cardoso foi encontrada morta em 28 de maio de 2024 , em Manaus. Ela ficou conhecida por interpretar a sinhazinha do Boi Garantido e foi uma das principais atrações do Festival de Parintins durante cinco anos.

Segundo o laudo preliminar citado na investigação, ela morreu após sofrer um edema cerebral, que comprometeu o funcionamento do coração e da respiração. O documento não apontou o que teria causado o edema.

A principal linha de investigação da polícia foi a possibilidade de uma overdose de cetamina.

Durante as investigações, policiais encontraram frascos da substância enterrados no quintal da casa de Djidja. Também foram apreendidas caixas de cetamina, seringas, frascos, bulas e cartelas de medicamentos.

Djidja Cardoso com a mãe Cleusimar Cardoso e o irmão Ademar Cardoso. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

articles.title: Chuvas intensas provocam alagamentos e interrompem travessia no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Quatro municípios registraram danos humanos ou materiais, segundo a Defesa Civil do estado. Mais de 160 pessoas foram afetadas, sendo 8 desabrigadas.
articles.summary: Quatro municípios registraram danos humanos ou materiais, segundo a Defesa Civil do estado. Mais de 160 pessoas foram afetadas, sendo 8 desabrigadas.
articles.body:
As chuvas que atingem o Rio Grande do Sul neste sábado (24) já provocam transtornos em diferentes regiões do estado.

Conforme o balanço preliminar da Defesa Civil divulgado neste sábado (24), 163 pessoas foram afetadas e oito ficaram desabrigadas em decorrência dos temporais. O monitoramento é realizado desde quarta-feira (21).

O levantamento aponta registros de ocorrências em quatro municípios , todos com danos humanos ou materiais associados às chuvas intensas. A cidade mais impactada foi Taquaruçu do Sul , onde 150 pessoas foram afetadas e duas vias ficaram bloqueadas.

Em Tucunduva , oito moradores precisaram deixar suas casas. O município também registrou dois imóveis alagados e uma via obstruída.

Chuvas no município Tucunduva — Foto: Divulgação/ Defesa Civil

Já em São Francisco de Assis , cinco pessoas foram atingidas pelos efeitos da chuva, que causou alagamento em uma residência e danos a uma obra pública de infraestrutura. Em Tenente Portela , houve registro de bloqueios em duas estradas locais.

Interior de Crissiumal enfrenta alagamentos

Chuva intensa no município de Crissiumal — Foto: Divulgação/ Guia Crissiumal

Em Crissiumal, na Região Noroeste, o acumulado de chuva ultrapassou 150 milímetros em menos de 24 horas , segundo a Defesa Civil municipal. O grande volume de água provocou o transbordamento de rios e riachos , resultando em alagamentos e interrupções de estradas no interior.

Também foram registrados danos em pontes e pontilhões . As localidades mais atingidas são Lajeado Crissiumal, Alto Crissiumal, Lajeado Grande, Mato Queimado e Esquina Tornquist, especialmente nas áreas próximas à divisa com Três Passos .

De acordo com o coordenador da Defesa Civil do município, Eduardo Fernandes, ainda não é possível calcular a dimensão total dos prejuízos . A avaliação deverá avançar somente quando o nível da água baixar, o que, conforme a previsão meteorológica, pode ocorrer entre segunda-feira (26) e terça-feira (27).

Apesar dos danos à infraestrutura e dos pontos de alagamento, não havia, até este sábado, registro de famílias isoladas ou de residências invadidas pela água.

Equipes da Secretaria de Obras atuam na liberação de estradas e no atendimento às áreas afetadas. A orientação é para que moradores evitem transitar por trechos alagados e mantenham atenção redobrada próximo a cursos d’água.

Cheia no município de Três Passos — Foto: Divulgação/ Três Passos News

Os efeitos da chuva também atingiram a ligação entre os municípios de Miraguaí e Três Passos. Na manhã deste sábado, a ponte sobre o Rio Turvo, entre as localidades de Água Fria e Romana Seca, voltou a ficar submersa em razão da elevação do nível do rio.

Com a estrutura coberta pela água, a passagem de veículos e pedestres foi interrompida. A expectativa é de que o volume do rio continue aumentando ao longo do dia, mantendo o bloqueio da travessia.

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) mantém um alerta de tempestade com grau de severidade classificado como grande perigo para áreas do Sul do país, incluindo o Noroeste gaúcho e a Região Celeiro.

Segundo o aviso, há possibilidade de chuva superior a 60 milímetros por hora ou mais de 100 milímetros em um dia, além de rajadas de vento acima de 100 km/h e risco de queda de granizo.

articles.title: Assédio eleitoral em Jacobina: Justiça determina suspensão imediata | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida atende a uma ação do Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT-BA). Em caso de descumprimento, a decisão prevê multa de R$ 50 mil para o município de Jacobina e de R$ 30 mil para o chefe de gabinete.
articles.summary: A Justiça determinou o fim do assédio eleitoral em Jacobina, sob pena de multa de R$ 50 mil, após denúncias de coação contra servidores municipais.
articles.body:
A Justiça do Trabalho determinou, em decisão liminar neste sábado (24), a suspensão imediata de práticas que podem caracterizar assédio eleitoral contra servidores e outros trabalhadores vinculados à Prefeitura de Jacobina , no norte da Bahia.

A medida atende a uma ação do Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT-BA) contra o município e o chefe de gabinete da prefeitura, Leopoldo Moraes Passos . O g1 entrou em contato com a gestão municipal para pedir um posicionamento, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Imagem aérea de Jacobina, no norte da Bahia — Foto: Prefeitura de Jacobina

Segundo o MPT, trabalhadores municipais teriam sido constrangidos a apoiar um determinado candidato nas eleições, sob ameaça de perda do emprego ou exclusão dos quadros da administração municipal . A ação aponta que Leopoldo Moraes Passos teria promovido reuniões e contatos com servidores para exigir a divulgação de propaganda política em perfis e status do WhatsApp, além de pressioná-los a votar em um candidato específico no segundo turno.

Na decisão, o juiz do trabalho Murilo Carvalho Sampaio Oliveira determinou que a prefeitura divulgue, até a meia-noite deste sábado, um comunicado oficial informando que o voto é livre e secreto e que nenhum trabalhador será obrigado a manifestar apoio político ou sofrerá consequências funcionais por sua escolha eleitoral. A determinação serve para:

A liminar também proíbe o município e o chefe de gabinete de convocar reuniões, realizar contatos pessoais, telefonemas ou enviar mensagens para pedir, orientar, induzir ou exigir apoio político de trabalhadores. Além disso, fica vedada a exigência de publicações em redes sociais, bem como a solicitação de fotos, vídeos ou qualquer outro meio de comprovação de voto.

O magistrado ressaltou que o voto secreto e a liberdade de escolha política são direitos garantidos pela Constituição Federal. Embora as denúncias ainda dependam de aprofundamento durante a instrução do processo, o juiz entendeu que os indícios apresentados pelo MPT e a proximidade da votação justificam a adoção imediata de medidas preventivas.

Em caso de descumprimento, a decisão prevê multa de R$ 50 mil para o município de Jacobina e de R$ 30 mil para Leopoldo Moraes Passos, além de multa de R$ 10 mil por hora de atraso no cumprimento das determinações.

O processo também foi encaminhado ao Ministério Público Eleitoral e ao Ministério Público da Bahia (MP-BA) para apuração de possíveis ilícitos eleitorais, criminais e atos de improbidade administrativa.

articles.title: Revisão Final do Enem 2026: Arena Batistão deve receber 8 mil alunos | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento deve reunir cerca de oito mil estudantes da rede estadual e do Pré-Uni.
articles.summary: A Revisão Final do Enem 2026 reunirá 8 mil estudantes na Arena Batistão, em Aracaju, consolidando o maior evento público e gratuito de preparação do país.
articles.body:
Gabarito de prova de concurso — Foto: Divulgação

Uma revisão pública preparatória para o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) será realizada no dia 6 de novembro, a partir das 15h, na Arena Batistão em Aracaju. Com o tema ‘Chegou a nossa vez!’, a iniciativa é promovida pelo Governo do Estado, por meio da Secretaria de Estado da Educação (Seed).

O evento deve reunir cerca de 8 mil estudantes, entre alunos da 3ª série do Ensino Médio da rede pública, do Programa Pré-Universitário (Pré-Uni) e das dez Diretorias Regionais de Educação (DREs) do estado, além de estudantes da 1ª e 2ª séries que participarão como treineiros.

Segundo a Seed, a programação do evento inclui aulas dinâmicas, resolução de questões e atividades interativas. Este ano, Sergipe registra mais de 20 mil estudantes inscritos para as provas do Enem.

Criado em 2000, o Programa Pré-Universitário da Seed completa 25 anos em 2026 consolidado como o maior programa público e gratuito de preparação para o Enem em Sergipe. Atualmente, conta com quase 5 mil alunos matriculados em 50 polos distribuídos por mais de 30 municípios. Ao longo de sua trajetória, a iniciativa já beneficiou mais de 100 mil estudantes e acumula marcas expressivas de aprovação em instituições de ensino superior.

articles.title: How London's Oxford Street was pedestrianised after years of failed attempts
articles.summary: More than a kilometre of the so-called "nation's high-street" will be pedestrianised from Monday.
articles.body:
On a bright, summer's day at City Hall in 2024, the mayor of London's senior advisers were in a room mulling over how to solve the most contentious of issues - getting vehicles off Oxford Street.

In the planning meeting, they were advocating a new approach.

The thorny issue of the pedestrianisation of London's most famous shopping street had foxed mayoral administrations for years.

Every time a new plan emerged, it was scrapped by Westminster Council, who owned the street and could be swayed by the marginal seats on either side of the debate.

Now the mayor's senior advisers were giving him another way he could end the impasse - using a development corporation.

The use of a development corporation for Oxford Street had actually been discussed in City Hall as far back as 2018 when yet another plan got scrapped.

Sadiq Khan had the pedestrianisation of Oxford Street in his 2016 manifesto and plans for it were advanced .

This followed a plan by locals to stand for election on the single-issue ticket of anti-pedestrianisation. In the face of such a challenge, the council changed its mind.

The proposal for making Oxford Street traffic-free had already been through a consultation and received the support of the council. London Mayor Lord Khan called the backtracking "a betrayal".

Creating a development corporation was a way around this.

It would mean a mayoral body taking control of how Oxford Street was developed while removing planning powers for the area from Westminster Council.

Three Westminster councillors would sit on the 12-person board, and one from Camden. The rest would be appointed by the mayor.

Having a development corporation in a central London semi-residential location would be unprecedented, with the method only previously being used to convert brownfield industrial areas at the Olympic Park and Old Oak Common.

Critics said it was anti-democratic and that it would disenfranchise local people, but the mayor said residents could not be allowed to hold up the development of the UK's main high street.

The Conservative leader of Westminster City Council accused Lord Khan of "cheating the system".

Even so the Oxford Street Development Corporation (OSDC) was created.

It has left many local residents feeling cut out of the democratic process. They fear the displacement of traffic on to their roads, with buses, taxis and bikes being rerouted to adjacent streets.

Karen Jones, who has lived in the area for 20 years, worries what will happen to their "beautiful garden neighbourhoods".

"You just cannot take 30 or 40 bus routes, and then switch them into green neighbourhoods with playgrounds and children, and expect they'll stay the same."

Michael Bolt, from the Marylebone Association, also feels the area's "fairly village atmosphere" will be ruined because "the traffic's just going to have to find ways around Oxford Street".

"Wigmore Street is going to be pretty well crushed with traffic, and traffic will then have to move up through Marylebone to try and get through."

He points out that when "this same plan came up in 2018, we were able to get rid of that as we had 54 democratically elected councillors, and it was for them to decide.

"Now we have a commission of 12 controlled mainly by him [Lord Khan] and he's able to push this through without us being able to have a say in it. Now it's impossible to exercise a democratic right."

Crucially, the creation of the OSDC and stripping the council of its powers required approval from the secretary of state for housing, communities and local government.

At the time, that was Angela Rayner. Prior to 2024, approval from a Conservative government was unlikely.

City Hall insiders say Rayner's backing was "great" and necessary for the creation of the OSDC.

They also say pedestrianisation is more than just the highway.

The mayor's vision needed a body to oversee the transformation and to create a cultural and retail destination, they argue.

And the creation of the OSDC was critical to that.

Nick Bowes, a former mayoral director at City Hall and now a partner at the communications agency LCA, says the 2024 general election had been key for the move as "everything changed, suddenly the political stars aligned".

He admits the use of a development corporation "isn't without controversy" as City Hall and the local authority, along with those it represents, consider the West End differently.

"City Hall and the government take a view that the economic contribution of the wider Oxford Street area is of strategic importance, not just to London but to the country as a whole.

"In their view, decisions about the future of the area can't just be taken at a local level based solely on local considerations.

"In this respect, OSDC is no different to other development corporations, and the reaction by some to the creation of a 'devco' as 'anti-democratic' is what was also seen in Stratford and west London."

Robin Smith runs a stall on Berwick Street. He thinks this is just the start of a process that will destroy the character of the West End.

"I think that closing Oxford Street will just move all the buses, the cabs, the motorcycles, the delivering vehicles, and the bicycles on to the backstreets, which are residential.

"So all of that congestion is going to go into smaller streets, which are less able to cope with it. And that's gonna create misery for anybody living north of Oxford Street, because their whole livelihood's going to be turned upside down by this."

He also fears small traders will end up being pushed out by larger corporate enterprises, along with the potential impact of more people coming to the area.

"I think it's tragic - 20,000 people coming [to the West End] in the evening is one thing, that's what Soho is and has always been.

"But if it's more like 200,000? That's the size of two Wembleys with no security and no sanitation. There's no public toilets, there's no facilities for this, so the whole thing crumbles."

The real work to transform Oxford Street won't start really until the spring. Over the busy Christmas period, work will not be possible.

Councillor Tim Barnes, deputy leader at Westminster Council, is worried that the plans are not fully-formed.

"We are concerned that some of the things that you'd expect at this point to have been resolved haven't yet been resolved. It's been the case right the way through this process that it's felt rushed, and it's felt under-resourced."

"Realistically, if we wanted this to be the best that it could be, we would have taken more time over it, and the mayor wouldn't have put this artificial deadline on things," he adds.

"We'd have had a much better scheme if we'd launched it next year. It feels rushed, it feels under-resourced, and it feels slightly undercooked."

Bowes thinks how the development corporation diverges from the local council will be important to watch.

Westminster Council has traditionally opposed anything over six storeys. Could the OSDC change that?

He says what is happening will be watched closely.

"To date, mayoral development corporations have been used as vehicles to drive regeneration over large areas of under-developed or brownfield land that is complicated by sitting astride the boundaries of two or more boroughs.

"Oxford Street is very different, covering a significantly smaller geographical area, which is primarily a high density, high land value retail and office area. There is no precedent that Oxford Street can copy.

"Many will be watching closely to see if the OSDC model can be applied elsewhere in London or beyond the M25," he explains.

When you ask advisers at City Hall if the mayor regards Oxford Street as his biggest legacy they don't deny it. They also point to the ultra low emission zone.

But certainly as a physical achievement in London, the mayor thinks his most significant achievement will be making a large part of the so-called "nation's high street" traffic-free.

articles.title: Reward offered over man's murder in Digbeth flat used as brothel
articles.summary: Jinming Zhang had been stabbed multiple times before he was found on 9 February 2022.
articles.body:
A £20,000 reward is being offered by Crimestoppers in connection with the murder of a man who was found dead in a Birmingham flat in 2022.

Jinming Zhang had been stabbed multiple times before he was found in the property, which police said was being used as a brothel, in Moseley Street in Digbeth.

West Midlands Police previously released CCTV of a suspect, while a DNA sample from the suspected killer found at the scene did not produce a match on the national database.

The case was featured in the BBC series of Forensics: The Real CSI last year, which revealed police believed the murder suspect may have sustained a hand injury in the frenzied attack.

Jenny Birch, who has been overseeing the investigation, urged anyone with information "no matter how small" to contact police.

"Someone out there knows something, and we won't give up until we have answers," she said.

"Mr Zhang was killed in such awful circumstances, and we will not stop until we find out who did this to him.

"People needn't be afraid to come forward with names. The DNA sample we have means that we are able to quickly and easily eliminate people from our ongoing investigation."

The motive was thought to have been robbery, although police have not been able to confirm that.

The masked suspect in the CCTV was described as black, in his late 20s at the time, about 5ft 4ins and of an average build.

He was captured wearing a dark hat and dark clothing as he walked along Barford Street just before the murder.

The DNA sample was submitted for forensic testing, which concluded that the suspect was a man and there was a 99.99% probability that he was black.

Crimestoppers said the reward was for information given anonymously that would lead to the conviction of the person responsible for the death of Zhang, a Chinese national.

articles.title: Nearly 1,000 arrested across France as police find potential weapons on protestors: officials
articles.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez says nearly 1,000 people were arrested as 70,000 police officers deployed across the country amid nationwide protests.
articles.body: Nearly 1,000 people were arrested Saturday as nationwide protests resumed, France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez told reporters. Earlier in the day, police officers preemptively searched protesters, and arrested people suspected of carrying potential weapons, including fireworks and ball bearings, Reuters reported. Nuñez did not specify where the arrests were made. In Paris, where police estimated 110,000 people marched, officers conducted more than 3,000 checks and arrested 65 people, the BBC reported. The French Interior Ministry said about 410,000 people participated in protests nationwide, while union organizers estimated attendance at 800,000. In Paris, union organizers put turnout at 250,000, compared with the police estimate of 110,000, according to CBS News. AMERICANS WARNED ABOUT PARIS TRAVEL AFTER VIOLENCE, LOOTING AND TEAR GAS-FILLED STREETS "Violent individuals have no place in the marches," the Paris Police Department said in a social media post. "The objective is clear: to prevent troublemakers from joining the procession, and to ensure the safety of the demonstrators." Central Paris resembled a city under lockdown, as shopkeepers boarded up storefronts, museums closed and more than 20 metro stations suspended service. In other cities — including Clermont-Ferrand, Grenoble, Lille and Nice — police have resorted to firing tear gas to break up unruly crowds, Reuters reported. Also in Nice, police used a water cannon to disperse a group of demonstrators who refused to pull back. And in Marseille and Lyon, there have been clashes between police officers and hooded youths. FRANCE’S TEEN RIOTS TAKE EXPLOSIVE NEW TURN AS GOVERNMENT POINTS FINGER AT HARD LEFT Some 70,000 police officers have been deployed across France to clamp down on agitators and prevent the kind of unrest seen during recent demonstrations, when cars were torched and the city hall building in Limoges was set on fire. Last weekend, more than 2,700 people were arrested during protests that later turned into riots and looting sprees. The nationwide marches were meant to reflect broader dissatisfaction with the French government, with protesters taking to the streets to air a range of different grievances. The protests began weeks earlier and were led by high school and university students. They were frustrated with teacher shortages and poor conditions at schools, including overcrowded classrooms and dilapidated buildings. articles.title: Thousands of people gather in support of Drumcree Orangemen
articles.summary: Hundreds of Orangemen are parading through Portadown, joined by bands and a crowd of supporters who have not been deterred by the weather.
articles.body:
Thousands of people have gathered in Portadown to show support for the Orange Order in the wake of the Drumcree dispute.

Hundreds of Orangemen paraded through the town centre, joined by bands and supporters who were not deterred by the stormy weather.

The parade comes amid continuing tensions surrounding the long-running Drumcree dispute, whereby the Orange Order has been banned from walking down the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road in the County Armagh town.

Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant banned the contentious parade on security advice after a stand-off between Orangemen and Garvaghy Road residents lasting almost two weeks.

This was the first major rally the Orange Order had held since a group of them were prevented by protesters from parading along the road in late September.

The scale of the crowd in Portadown appeared to surprise even the most optimistic of organisers.

Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) MP Carla Lockhart was there, while her party colleagues and assembly members Jonathan Buckley and Brian Kingston paraded with their lodges.

The Drumcree dispute has led to divisions within the unionist party, with Lockhart standing down as party officer on Thursday. She said the DUP had it "within its gift to remove" Michelle O'Neill as Northern Ireland's first minister.

This would mean removing DUP Deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly from her role, as the two ministers share an office and cannot function without one another.

O'Neill had taken part in the Garvaghy Road protests and earlier this week, the Sinn Féin politician attended police interviews over her involvement .

The first part of the parade was followed by a series of speeches, mainly from members of the Orange Order.

This was very much an Orange Order event and not a political rally but inevitably there was a political tone to many of the comments.

There was explicit criticism of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) Chief Constable Jon Boutcher, the secretary of state and the first minister, but also implicit criticism of the leaders of the two biggest unionist parties - the DUP and Ulster Unionist Party.

Traditional Unionist Voice leader Jim Allister was applauded but by far the loudest cheers were for the Orange Order's legal adviser Jamie Bryson and the local MP Lockhart.

She was invited on to the stage and presented with a special gift for her support of the Orangemen.

Lockhart was the only politician to take to the stage, where she repeated her challenge to the DUP leadership: "Profound consequences must mean profound consequences. Michelle O'Neill must go.

"That's where I stand, and this lady is not for turning."

Portadown District Master Nigel Dawson warned politicians that they could face consequences at the next election over the Drumcree dispute.

"Politicians need to remember that we put them into office and we can take them out of office," he said.

He added that the Orange Order had won the right "to return home via our traditional route and Portadown District intends to exercise that right on a date and time of our choosing, and if necessary, without further recourse".

Orange Order Deputy District Master Alistair Power said Drumcree must not be allowed to divide unionism.

"It should not be used by parties to attack each other publicly over differences of opinion," he added. "We need to stand united."

The Drumcree parade dispute began in the mid-1990s and it almost derailed the peace process at the time.

Violence related to the dispute resulted in riots, roadblocks and murders.

When the Orange Order was prevented by police from walking down the route in July 1995 there was a tense stand-off. It was the same for the next three years.

The Parades Commission began operating in 1998 to regulate parades and try to defuse tension around marches.

Its decision not to allow a march down the Garvaghy Road that summer has been challenged by the order for the past three decades.

Last month, the Parades Commission decided that the march could go ahead on 27 September with restrictions in place after its original decision to stop the march was overturned in court.

That morning, up to 1,000 people - including nationalist politicians - blocked the road, preventing Orangemen marching from Drumcree Church a mile to the west.

Since then there were repeated attempts by the Orange Order to walk the route, but they were stopped by police.

Residents maintained a constant presence on the Garvaghy Road, but that ended on 9 October when the NI secretary banned the parade following advice from the PSNI chief constable.

On 12 October, the Garvaghy Road residents failed in a bid to challenge the Parades Commission's decision to allow the Drumcree parade to walk down the predominantly nationalist road.

The Court of Appeal judges said their decision was confined to the lawfulness of the decision - it was not deciding whether or not the march should occur.

Lady Chief Justice Dame Siobhan Keegan said the ruling was decided before Sir Chris banned the parade.

Sir Chris's decision is being challenged in the courts .

articles.title: Set to expand cabinet, J&K CM Omar Abdullah asks hopefuls not to ‘mob or spam’ him
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah, who met lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha Saturday and announced that the much-anticipated cabinet expansion will take place
articles.body: SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah, who met lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha Saturday and announced that the much-anticipated cabinet expansion will take place next week, has urged party colleagues to stop sending him lengthy WhatsApp messages and book-length profiles seeking ministerial berths.He also advised them against knocking on his doors or that of his father and National Conference president, Dr Farooq Abdullah, to lobby for ministerial positions.After meeting Sinha, Omar told reporters he sought an appointment with him for next week so that he can make changes and expand his council of ministers.“Now that I have told you about the reshuffle, I want to make a request to my colleagues. There is no need to knock on Farooq Abdullah’s door, my door or anyone else’s door,” Omar said. “The decision about who will become a minister has been taken. I request my colleagues to be patient. First, it is in God’s hands and then we took the decision. Whoever is destined to become a minister will become one,” he said.“I am receiving so many WhatsApp messages, with people writing lengthy resumes and sending me entire book-length profiles. It is as if I do not know these people. They are sending me their complete biodata, as though I am not already familiar with them,” he said. “So please, do not send WhatsApp messages.”Omar was sworn in on Oct 16, 2024, along with five ministers, including deputy CM Surinder Choudhary. At present, three cabinet berths remain vacant.Under the norms, the strength of the council of ministers cannot exceed nine or 10% of the total strength of the 90-member assembly.Meanwhile, the opposition described Omar’s public “advice” to ministerial hopefuls as demeaning to the political class and called it as “the cult of self.”Leader of opposition, BJP’s Sunil Sharma, who has been claiming that NC will “implode” if Omar went ahead with cabinet expansion, said, “The CM is behaving like a king. He doesn’t like people visiting his home. He is out to demean his own MLAs and has repeatedly humiliated them inside and outside the Assembly.”Peoples Conference chairman Sajad Lone called Omar’s statement “the cult of self.” “I watched CM sahib talking to the media after meeting LG sahib. What a contemptuous and disdainful way of asking his party MLAs to not pester him for a ministerial berth. I honestly can’t believe these MLAs are comfortable with such belittling and humiliating remarks,” Lone said.“If you are unable to accommodate them in the cabinet, you can spare them the public humiliation,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Thousands booked tropical Bahamas cruise and ended up in freezing Canada instead
articles.summary: Royal Caribbean's Oasis of the Seas rerouted over 5,000 Bahamas-bound passengers to Halifax, Nova Scotia, after stormy weather forced an itinerary change.
articles.body: A cruise scheduled to sail to the sunny Bahamas this week took a northward turn for the worse when it got rerouted to chilly Canada instead. More than 5,000 passengers boarded Royal Caribbean’s Oasis of the Seas in New Jersey on Oct. 18, expecting a seven-day cruise to Florida and the Bahamas. But forecasts of stormy weather off the East Coast prompted the cruise line to change the itinerary, sending the ship north to Halifax, Nova Scotia, according to reports. The ship stopped in Halifax for about 24 hours, giving passengers time to explore ashore, shop and take harbor rides. It departed Wednesday evening and is scheduled to return to New Jersey on Sunday after three days at sea. OUTRAGED CRUISE PASSENGERS SOUND OFF ABOUT 'IMMENSE DISAPPOINTMENT' AFTER ABRUPT CANCELLATION The line announced the changed itinerary the evening before the ship sailed, according to reports, leaving passengers with little time to adjust. "My husband said to me, 'This is a joke, right?'" New Jersey resident Marie Durning told CTV News. "I have my winter hat and earmuffs, but I forgot my scarf," she said, adding that she was left scrambling to repack. Daytime temperatures hovered in the upper 40s to low 50s this week in Halifax, with overnight lows in the 30s, according to weather reports. ANGRY CRUISE PASSENGERS SAY FRUSTRATING ISSUE SHOULD HAVE BEEN DISCLOSED BEFORE BOOKING For some, the surprise destination was a chance to make the most of an unfamiliar city. "I’m grateful and I’m going to make the best of it," Jim Matthews, who lives near Paterson, New Jersey, told the outlet. "And I have found out that Halifax is a beautiful city." But not everyone was onboard. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "I am already from Canada, and I wanted to go to the Bahamas," Nicholas Meli, who drove seven hours with his family from Toronto to New Jersey to board, told CTV News. Online, commenters in Reddit’s r/canada thread expressed sympathy for the passengers but also shared their fondness for Halifax. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS One commenter called it their favorite Canadian city to visit, but said they would be "bummed" to end up there while expecting a Bahamas beach vacation. Another summed up the change more bluntly, writing, "Halifax is gorgeous, but it is not the Bahamas." Weather and other circumstances can prompt Royal Caribbean to alter or substitute ports, according to its website, and it is not necessarily required to refund fares or provide compensation. articles.title: Farooq Abdullah's comments on Pakistan and Kashmir draw flak
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah on Saturday declared that Pakistan had “saved” Kashmiris by keeping the issue alive at
articles.body: SRINAGAR: National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah on Saturday declared that Pakistan had “saved” Kashmiris by keeping the issue alive at international forums, while being careful to say that “otherwise their (Pakistan’s) intentions are not good”.His statement drew flak from BJP, which slammed it as “seditious and anti-national”.“If you do not remain (committed to NC), you will be erased. Even our identity will disappear. Nothing will be left. They are silent today because there is noise in the world and our neighbour is constantly behind it. Everywhere they say ‘the decision regarding Kashmir has not been made’. That is what is saving us…,” Farooq told a meeting of NC workers in Baramulla. The words “they” and “their” were seen as an allusion to the Centre.Farooq’s son, J&K chief minister Omar Abdullah, had not reacted to his father’s remarks till late Saturday.Farooq urged NC workers and legislators to remain loyal to the party, whether in power or not, as he touched on a range of issues in his speech. “Hold on to the truth. Speaking the truth is not easy, but unless you remain truthful and stand up for what is right, your future will never be secure,” the veteran said.Citing the 1947 tribal invasion, Farooq condemned the “atrocities” inflicted on Kashmiris by the raiders from Pakistan”. He paid tributes to Maqbool Sherwani, an NC worker who died staving off the intruders, saying his “sacrifice helped stop the raiders in Baramulla and save Kashmir”.Farooq also mentioned the Chittisinghpura massacre in which 36 Sikhs were killed in south Kashmir on March 20, 2000, during then US President Bill Clinton’s visit to India. He said a subsequent judicial inquiry had found that five men accused of carrying out the killings were not the perpetrators but shopkeepers “who had been picked up by police and killed”. According to Farooq, the inquiry judge should have investigated the massacre itself but was “told from Delhi” not to.BJP decried Farooq’s comments. Party functionary Ravinder Raina called them “treason” and asked how Pakistan could ever be a well-wisher of the people of J&K. “Farooq Abdullah chose Baramulla for his pro-Pakistan remarks just two days after the anniversary of Pakistan’s Oct 22, 1947 invasion of J&K. This is the land of Maqbool Sherwani, who stood against invaders, not a stage to whitewash Pakistan’s bloody history,” J&K BJP spokesman Sajid Yousuf Shah said.Peoples Conference’s Imran Reza Ansari cautioned against following Farooq. “If a common Kashmiri speaks in a similar tone, govt will in seconds put that person in detention under PSA or UAPA. Please save your children and your families. Don’t emulate this person,” Ansari said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mellon Foundation donates $750,000 grant to University of California to establish South Asian American studies centre
articles.summary: The University of California, Santa Barbara has received a $750,000 grant from the Mellon Foundation to establish a nationally focused, interdisciplinary
articles.body: The University of California, Santa Barbara has received a $750,000 grant from the Mellon Foundation to establish a nationally focused, interdisciplinary centre for South Asian American studies, aiming to give the field a more structured academic foundation and address a longstanding lack of institutional support. The project was initiated after the foundation approached the university in August last year. It will be led by Jigna Desai and Sameer Pandya, professors in UCSB’s Department of Asian American Studies.Pandya, who chairs the department, is also a bestselling novelist, while Desai is the inaugural director of the university’s Center for Feminist Futures.Desai said having two specialists in South Asian American studies within the same Asian American studies department was unusual."It's a real rarity to have two people who do South Asian American studies in an Asian American studies department," she said.The grant seeks to address a gap in higher education. Although Asian American studies programs have expanded across the US over the past two decades, dedicated resources for South Asian American studies research remain limited. Scholars in the field often lack established academic pathways, specialised coursework and structured mentorship.“In a way, the field has been in existence for 30 years in a space between post-colonial studies…and the rise of Asian American Studies,” Pandya said. “And so there’s never been a clear, dedicated space for South Asian American studies.”One of the centre's priorities will be to expand research into issues that have received less attention within broader Asian American studies, including caste and its role in the South Asian diaspora.While caste has long been studied in the context of the South Asian subcontinent, its influence on migrant communities and across generations of South Asians living in the US and Europe requires further examination."Caste is one of those categories, and specifically caste in relation to migration, but also how it plays a highly present force in shaping people's lives in the diaspora," Desai said.Over the next four years, the $750,000 grant will support initiatives in four areas: undergraduate curriculum development and learning opportunities, graduate training and research support, mentorship for junior faculty, and partnerships with public-facing projects.Planned programmes include open-access online curricula, summer internships for undergraduates, dissertation fellowships and manuscript workshops.The broader aim is to bring together a field whose researchers have often worked independently and establish a lasting academic community connecting senior scholars, early-career faculty members and students."We like the collective noisiness of the current conversation in a way that before we were all just working on our own, trying to figure it all out," Pandya said.The centre's inaugural event brought together 20 scholars from across the US for a symposium examining power, dominance and complicity within South Asian American studies.The gathering helped strengthen connections among researchers at different career stages and included workshops to develop scholarship for a forthcoming edited collection on critical South Asian American studies..UCSB's interdisciplinary Department of Asian American Studies is part of the broader Ethnic Studies tradition. articles.title: Soldiers guard center of Milan as thousands of protesters march across European cities
articles.summary: Thousands of young people marched Saturday through the streets of Milan, where large numbers of soldiers were deployed and luxury boutiques were boarded up in case of a repeat of last weekend’s chaotic looting and clashes.
articles.body: MILAN — Thousands of young people marched Saturday through the streets of Milan, where large numbers of soldiers were deployed and luxury boutiques were boarded up in case of a repeat of last weekend’s chaotic looting and clashes. Premier Giorgia Meloni announced a raft of measures, including sending an additional 500 soldiers to Milan and tougher penalties for minors, who police said made up a large part of the violent protesters last week. While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities Saturday from Milan to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana. The protests encompass a broad range of issues from education and corruption to anti-war movements, pensions and housing. Army vehicles and boarded-up luxury stores in Milan In Milan, huge crowds of mostly young people gathered as night fell, chanting insults to Meloni and holding aloft banners such as “No to lies of the state.” A group of protesters dumped manure outside Italy’s energy regulator and burned a symbolic, oversized electricity bill, images broadcast on local television showed. The 500 soldiers deployed to Milan came in addition to hundreds already stationed there, supporting about 5,000 police and other security personnel. Authorities used drone surveillance, checks at railway stations, rapid-response units and online monitoring for potential calls to violence. Milan Mayor Giuseppe Sala has said he is concerned about a repeat of violence and expressed support for the deployment of more soldiers. Many stores, particularly luxury boutiques within Milan’s fashion district including Omega, Tiffany and Gucci, boarded up their front windows. Rioters last weekend smashed their way into stores, targeting sneakers, athletic wear and sporting goods on streets that run off the city’s central Duomo square. Security measures extended beyond the city center over concerns protesters could move into other neighborhoods. Demonstrations also took place in Rome, Turin and other cities, with some turning violent. Officials said Saturday they were investigating a 30-year-old freelance journalist said to be the “mastermind” of the newly formed October 17 movement, which has been the main driver of the recent protests in Italy. Milan police say last week’s violence and looting involved about 2,000 very young protesters, many of them “naturalized, second-generation Italians,” alongside foreign nationals. Over two days, police arrested 45 people, including 34 minors. “Many young people increasingly lack a sense of belonging and prospects for the future. Part of our society feels excluded, amid social and economic inequalities,” Milan’s welfare councilor, Lamberto Bertolé, told The Associated Press. Defense Minister Guido Crosetto said the soldiers deployed Saturday were only recently allowed to use plastic restraint ties and only in areas around train stations, not throughout the city. They are not authorized to carry pepper spray or tasers, he said. Protesters try to force entry into Colosseum in Rome Security was also heightened in Rome, where authorities locked down luxury shopping streets and stepped up controls around the Circus Maximus and Piazza del Popolo. A small number of protesters tried to force their way into the Colosseum, but were ushered out by guards. Elsewhere, several hundred students demonstrated peacefully to stress they were not rioters. “I think the images from last week were truly something terrible, especially for the young people, for the students, for the vast majority of the younger generations who want to study ... and do not accept being represented by those who use issues and needs to devastate entire cities,” said Riccardo Ponzio, national president of an Italian far-right student association. A separate anti-war march took off in central Rome. Organizers sought to distance themselves from potential unrest, urging participants to keep their faces uncovered and hands visible. Clashes and buildings set on fire in Albania In Albania’s capital Tirana, riot police used water cannons on large groups of protesters, some of whom set government buildings on fire and threw projectiles at police. Authorities said 2,500 officers patrolled the streets Saturday. For over a week, protesters have hurled rocks, flares, firebombs and fireworks at police who have used batons and tear gas in clashes in the city center. High school and university students are demanding lower tuition fees, greater state investment in education and protesting corruption in the education system. Some have joined a broader anti-government movement calling for the resignation of Socialist Prime Minister Edi Rama. A separate protest organized by the opposition outside the prime minister’s office turned violent earlier, with some activists lighting fires on the street. Rama said Saturday his government was preparing a response to the students’ demands and called them to a dialogue. He warned that violent protesters will face penalties. Retirees march in Madrid over pensions Thousands of retirees and others marched in Spain’s capital Saturday to demand public pensions aren’t meddled with. Large crowds marched peacefully down streets in central Madrid, waving colorful flags and banners reading “protect pensions” and “decent pensions for today and the future.” “They are threatening us with privatizing pensions. It’s just another thing they want to profit from,” said Maria José Benito, 68. The protests came ahead of next month’s snap election as Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist Party criticized the conservative opposition Popular Party for making overtures about privatizing public pensions. Spain also has been roiled by protests this fall around the issue of housing, as rental and home costs have risen in recent years beyond what many Spaniards can afford. Affordable housing is main theme in Lisbon protests Taking their cue from Spaniards, protesters in Lisbon demanding affordable housing marched across the city on Saturday. They have also targeted recent measures announced by the government of Prime Minister Luis Montenegro that include easing the cap on yearly rent increases and facilitating the eviction of tenants who fail to pay rent. Montenegro defends the measures saying that it aims at reinforcing trust between tenants and landlords and boosting the rentals market. Protesters claim that the measures are not balanced and put tenants in a more vulnerable position.

articles.title: In 2007, an Ohio couple bought a home and the husband died two years later; after three loan modifications and a $449,905 foreclosure claim, an October 22 court upheld the bank's right to foreclose
articles.summary: An Ohio appeals court has upheld a lender's right to enforce a $449,905 (£346,000) foreclosure judgment against a home in Cuyahoga County.
articles.body: An Ohio appeals court has upheld a lender's right to enforce a $449,905 (£346,000) foreclosure judgment against a home in Cuyahoga County. The ruling ends a 17-year legal and financial dispute involving three separate loan modifications. The decision, issued on 22 October 2026 by the Eighth District Court of Appeals of Ohio, rejects arguments made by homeowner Sandra Doberdruk. It confirms that Wells Fargo Bank, the mortgage holder, has the legal right to collect the debt through foreclosure. Court records show that Doberdruk and her late husband bought the property in July 2007 and took out a mortgage to pay for the home. Her husband died two years later. After his death, Doberdruk faced serious financial difficulties, leading to repeated notices of missed payments and several agreements to change the loan terms.Three loan modifications across fifteen yearsTo avoid immediate foreclosure after her husband's death, Doberdruk entered into several formal agreements to change the terms of her mortgage with the loan servicer. According to filings published by the Eighth District Court of Appeals, the first two loan modifications took place in 2009 and 2014. They changed monthly principal payments and lowered interest rates. However, Doberdruk continued to struggle with payments, leading to a third loan modification in 2022. The 2022 agreement clearly referred to the original 2007 promissory note and mortgage signed by both spouses. It confirmed the existing debt obligations and combined unpaid interest with a revised total principal balance. Despite the third modification, the payments fell behind again. Wells Fargo then began formal foreclosure proceedings in the Cuyahoga County Court of Common Pleas.Court rejects challenge to standing and default claimsIn her appeal against the magistrate judge's foreclosure order, Doberdruk argued that the bank did not have the legal right to foreclose. She claimed there were problems with the records showing how the mortgage had been transferred between parties. She also argued that her late husband's estate had to be included in the case. Writing for the three-judge appeals panel, the Eighth District Court of Appeals rejected these arguments. The judges said that signing the 2022 loan modification confirmed the existing mortgage security and supported Wells Fargo's status as the legal holder of the loan note. The court explained that when a surviving homeowner signs a loan modification that refers to an existing mortgage on property they own, they become personally responsible for the revised terms. The ruling also confirmed that the bank had met all legal requirements under Ohio property law. It provided the original promissory note, the recorded mortgage and a verified account showing the unpaid balance of $449,905. The panel also found that ownership of the property had passed directly to Doberdruk after her husband's death. As a result, his probate estate no longer had an interest in the home, meaning it did not need to be included in the lawsuit.Affirmed judgment and property sale protocolThe appeals court upheld the lower court's summary judgment, allowing the Cuyahoga County Sheriff's Department to move forward with the court-ordered public auction of the property. Under Ohio civil procedure, money raised from the sheriff's sale will first go toward outstanding court administration fees and unpaid county property taxes. articles.title: Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
articles.summary: Officials have so far managed to avoid a repeat of last weekend's rioting and looting as hundreds of thousands took part in demonstrations.
articles.body:
Nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France which were followed by some clashes late on Saturday, officials have said.

After a day of largely peaceful demonstrations, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux.

But officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France's modern history.

The interior ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000.

Katya Adler: France divided over who to blame for riots and what to learn from them

Some 70,000 police officers were deployed and restrictions imposed in several cities to prevent the latest protests over the cost of living and poor school conditions from descending into the kind of chaos which saw officers outnumbered, hundreds of businesses looted and buildings torched.

President Emmanuel Macron had decreed earlier this week that only demonstrations organised by a recognised trade unions would be permitted. Hundreds of people have been jailed for vandalism, arson and looting after fast-track court hearings in recent days.

Clashes between protesters and riot police in Paris erupted at the end of a peaceful march from the city's Porte d'Italie towards Porte de Vincennes on Saturday, where the police operation included an elite unit that usually deals with organised crime and counter-terrorism.

Some protesters were seen erecting makeshift barricades and pelting officers with projectiles, while police baton-charged groups of masked youths who were smashing the windows of a car dealership.

French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that "several thousand radical activists gathered at the rear of the march, including around 500 individuals identified as rioters", the AFP news agency reported.

In the southern port of Marseille, rubbish bins were set ablaze and metal sheets used to block streets. A law enforcement vehicle was seen driving through a burning barricade in France's second-largest city.

Meanwhile, some protesters in dark clothing and face coverings were seen taking boards off a building to build a street barricade in the southern city of Bordeaux.

In Lyon, police used tear gas grenades to disperse a crowd which had reportedly gathered in an area deemed off-limits by the local prefecture.

"There were around 150 of us, mostly secondary school and university students. Then the tear gas came almost immediately. You could barely see anything in the street," said one protester in France's third-largest city.

Nuñez said late in the day that nearly 1,000 people had been arrested, a number he said would increase.

The minister also said two people had been "seriously injured": one in the south-western city of Toulouse, and another one in Clermont-Ferrand, central France.

Earlier, a peaceful protester in Paris who gave her name as Zelie told the BBC people had taken to the streets because they were "really frustrated" and had been "suffering a lot" since Macron came to office.

"They keep us quiet. They take our money, they tax us a lot and we can't say anything. Today we are in the streets because it's been too long, it's been too much," the 26-year-old said.

Two masked teenage protesters, who did not want to give their names, also said their generation was in despair and felt abandoned by the government.

"I think looting is really not good," one of the demonstrators said of last Saturday's disorder. "But it's because of poverty and the violence of the police."

He added that the protests would end "when we have a response to our demands. We really want a change in France".

Meanwhile, some 13,000 people joined a rally against the hard-right National Rally party in the north-central city of Orléans which proceeded peacefully.

Mass protests triggered by similar issues as in France also rocked several other European cities on Saturday.

In Albania's capital Tirana, riot police fired tear gas to disperse thousands of anti-government demonstrators, while clashes were also reported in Belgium's capital Brussels.

In Milan, northern Italy, a major security operation including hundreds of soldiers alongside police prevented protesters gathering in the city. Many had feared a repeat of violent scenes last week when some started fires, smashed windows and looted shops.

Around 550,000 people took part in last weekend's demonstrations against rising fuel prices and the cost of living, with frustrations escalating after weeks of student protests. The chaos which followed resulted in more than 2,500 arrests.

Marches were initially largely peaceful but became marred by scenes of violence, looting and destruction, with more than 2,000 shops and other businesses across France said to have been directly impacted. The damage was estimated "at hundreds of millions euros", France's Chambers of Commerce and Industry (CCI) said.

One demonstrator's hand was blown off by a police crowd-control grenade, according to the AFP news agency, while about 1,000 police officers were injured.

The French authorities later said they were forced to impose overnight curfews in Paris and other cities.

The continuing protests come ahead of France's presidential elections in six months' time, and leading contenders have levelled the blame at Macron and his ministers.
